source: forgesworn/quench docs/LANES.md (locked at a9f61ae, amendment 1) and docs/EVIDENCE.md, Q10 verdict
purpose: Evidence for Oathrun's model-selection table (docs/MODEL-ROUTING-GOALS.md, G3b): how often each cheaper lane delivers an accepted result, at what cost and time, next to DeepSeek V4 Pro. Evidence, not authority: it does not review or activate an Oathrun lane.

harness.client: Claude Code 2.1.281 headless, Q5 held-out flags and disallowed tools, effort medium
harness.route: Ollama daemon's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (cloud tags proxied to ollama.com)
harness.acceptance: deterministic checkers (and a scope check for code), no model reviewer
harness.tasks: Q5 held-out pack on commander.js and markdown-it, plain arm: orientation, diagnosis, impact, code change (2 tasks x 3 repetitions per class); Q8 chains under carry: six dependent steps per repository, 3 repetitions
harness.notOathrun: Measures model capability on these tasks, not an Oathrun lane, journey, disclosure boundary or provider-policy standing.

qwen3.8:latest.role: withdrawn after two probes (M4, no token charge)
qwen3.8:latest.reason: About 40 minutes a session on a host that serves one request at a time and also serves a live agent; per-turn latency at long context, not thinking, sets the pace. Qualifying would take about 30 hours to show a saving of cents per task against Flash.

findings: Flash matched Pro on every class and on dependent chains at about a fifth of Pro's cost per accepted result.
GLM matched Pro too, at about two fifths of Pro's cost and more slowly (code change median 810 s against Flash's 242 s).
On this Ollama build (0.34.2), a request with no thinking control lets Qwen 3.8 think; only an explicit disabled setting turns it off. A lane that sends no control is thinking.
Markdown-it chain step 4 under carry was accepted once in nine runs across all three lanes: a task to review, not a lane difference.
limits: Two repositories, three repetitions, one harness.
No frontier baseline was run (owner's decision): the lanes are shown to match DeepSeek Pro, not a frontier model.
Costs are estimates from reported tokens at published rates, not invoices.
